main_result.statement: Let p=y-R(x), q=a(p)z-H(p,x), R in C[x] of degree at least2, a in C[p] nonconstant, H arbitrary in C[p,x]. If f,g,h belong to C[p,q] and their original (x,y,z) Jacobian is nilpotent, their speed field has transcendence degree at most1.
main_result.proof: Rank2 forces the coefficient minor Jfg nonzero. The reverse determinant forces H=A(p)R(x)+B(p)x+C(p). If a'A-aA' is nonzero, highest trace degrees force f_q=g_q=0. Otherwise A=k a; the reduced trace rules out all branches except a quadratic resonance, whose mixed-partial identity forces g_q=c/a for nonzero complex c, incompatible with polynomial coefficient membership.
main_result.strengthening: No nonlinear-specialization hypothesis or restriction on the base dependence of H remains in the polynomial-coefficient theorem.
main_result.limits: No rank-one classification, arbitrary nonlinear-intercept normal form, or cancellation recognition. The actual W=u application is diagnostic within an already-polynomial A.

rational_classification.statement: All rational coefficient rank2 solutions are quadratic: R=(r/2)x^2+s*x+t, H=k*a*R+B*x+C, D=B/a with D' nonzero; f=f0-c*D/r, g=g0+c*(q+C)/a-c*k*p-c*s*D/r, h=h0+k*g-c*D^2/(2*r), with r,c nonzero constants.
rational_classification.converse: Coefficient trace and reverse determinant vanish, so (BA)^2=0 and (AB)^3=0. The coefficient Jacobian minor is -c^2*D'/(r*a).
rational_classification.ambient_polynomiality: Exactly D in C[p]. Ambient polynomiality is weaker than membership of all speeds in C[p,q].
rational_classification.actual_boundary: p=y-x^2/2, q=pz-p^2x, speeds=(-p,q/p,-p^2/2). The displayed four-coordinate line family has a two-sided polynomial inverse. It violates coefficient-subring membership, not the theorem.
